title: Identifying Immovable Obstructions
question: Which of the following is considered an immovable obstruction, entitling you to free relief under the Rules?

choices.text: A path with an artificial (man-made) surface
A pile of leaves gathered by the wind
A divot hole in the fairway

explanation: A path with a man-made surface is classed as an immovable obstruction. You are allowed free relief from it. The other options are either loose impediments, natural damage, or animal holes.

juniorVersion.title: What Counts as Something You Can’t Move on the Golf Course?
juniorVersion.question: Which of these is a thing on the course that you can't move, and you can get a free drop if your ball is stuck on it?

choices.text: A path made with concrete or tarmac
A pile of leaves blown together by the wind
A hole where grass has been taken out
A hill made by a mole

juniorVersion.explanation: A path made out of concrete or tarmac is something put there by people and you can't move it. If your ball is on it or it makes it hard to take a swing, you can get a free drop. The other things are natural or loose, not man-made and fixed.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Something on the course that is man-made and stuck in place, like a path or a sprinkler. You can’t move it, and you can get a free drop if it gets in your way.
This means you can move your ball away without getting a penalty if the rules let you.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Help children spot things on the course that are made by people and can’t be moved, like paths or drains, and remind them that they can take a free drop if these get in their way.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think anything in their way, like leaves or animal holes, always lets them drop for free.
Kids may try to move things that are fixed in place, or think they can’t get relief from something man-made and stuck.
